finding: Silver is your largest exposure: 22% of the portfolio across 4 holdings.
detail: The silver fund-of-funds invest in silver ETFs, so these holdings move almost identically and add little diversification over holding one. A single commodity at this weight makes the portfolio swing with silver prices.
consider: Decide what share of the portfolio you want in precious metals; one vehicle may be enough.

finding: 61% of your equity is in mid- and small-cap funds and stocks; large caps are 16%.
detail: Mid and small caps can grow faster but usually fall further in market corrections.
consider: Check that this tilt matches how much short-term volatility you can sit through.

finding: You hold 3 small-cap funds and 2 mid-cap funds.
detail: Funds in the same category often own many of the same companies, so extra funds add complexity more than diversification.
consider: Compare their portfolios; one or two per category is usually enough.

finding: 9 stocks make up 9% of the portfolio; 8 are below your purchase price.
detail: Most are small companies, with positions of a few thousand rupees each, so they barely move the total but need following.
consider: Review each against why you bought it, using the news and results below.

finding: Sector / thematic funds are 14% of the portfolio.
detail: A single-sector fund rises and falls with that industry.
consider: Keep sector funds to a size you are comfortable seeing swing.

finding: Debt and hybrid funds are 5% of the portfolio.
detail: These usually cushion falls in stocks and metals.
consider: Think about whether you want a larger cushion for money you may need in the next few years.
